title: Debrief / Review — flow inspiration
intro: Product-first flow gallery for the Essentials 2.0 debrief and review module: rewatching recorded simulation sessions, a QR-to-phone second screen for faculty, AI debrief summaries and clips, recording the debrief itself, group grading, and downloading or sharing recordings. Access to recordings from a course, live control during recording and the general mobile app are covered by other modules. Sources: Mobbin (web and iOS) and Refero (web). Researched 30 September 2026.
baseline: The SRV (LearningSpace session video review) is reused: video on the left, right-panel tabs Annotation, Data Entry, Layout and Transcript, a chaptered timeline with clickable manual and AI annotation markers, and a speaker-labelled, searchable transcript. Today faculty annotations are visible to learners on the debrief-room screen, which faculty dislike. The concept: when the recording ends, the SRV shows a QR for the debrief; faculty scan it and get a web page on their phone with their own annotations, AI annotations, the AI summary and AI clips, while the big screen shows only the video, controlled from the phone. The debrief audio is captured and AI-harvested, with a phone voice memo as fallback.

jobs.title: Rewatch videos
jobs.description: Jump to moments from markers/chapters/transcript, playback speed, multi-angle, resume where you left off

jobs.title: Separate app or QR: see notes and annotations
jobs.description: Scan a QR on the big screen → phone becomes the private remote/notes view while the big screen shows only video; handoff between devices

jobs.title: AI-based debriefing (formative & summative)
jobs.description: AI summary of what happened, suggested discussion points, evidence-linked moments, faculty edit/approve before showing

jobs.title: AI-provided short clips
jobs.description: Auto-generated highlight clips/reels from long recordings, trimming, reviewing and publishing clips

jobs.title: Record the debriefing and attach the evaluation to reports
jobs.description: Record the discussion itself (audio), transcribe, attach outcomes/grades to the session record

jobs.title: Group grading
jobs.description: Grade/give feedback to a whole team at once with per-person overrides; rubric for a group

jobs.title: Download videos / easy sharing of recordings
jobs.description: Share link with expiry and permissions, share with a specific learner, download with a consent/confirmation step

jobs.title: 360 camera / PTZ in review
jobs.description: Switching camera angles or a 360 view during playback

products.name: Grain
products.why: The closest twin of the SRV: AI outcomes and action items carry timestamps that jump the video, transcript search is synced to a speaker talk-time timeline, and a rubric scorecard is filled in under the video and sent to one named learner. The AI summary is live with Share before anyone approves it.

products.name: Fireflies
products.why: The only product that previews AI output on past meetings before the AI runs for real, and the clearest human-finalised clip: drag-select against the highlighted transcript, then a title and 'Who can access' before Done.

products.name: Canva
products.why: The only flow that shows the big-screen side of a QR handoff: a large QR plus short code, a live participant count and a Hide toggle that clears the join banner from the public display. The phone side hands out remote control by QR or link, with Pause.

products.name: Google TV
products.why: Phone as the full transport remote: 'Watch on TV' hands playback to the big screen, a persistent 'Living Room TV' bar confirms the connection, and the scrubber and ±30s skips live only on the phone.

products.name: Otter AI
products.why: Phone capture of a conversation with a live transcript and one-tap highlight, comment and photo markers while recording. Its web review is the module's counter-example: the AI summary can be copied, shared or posted to Slack with no edit or approve step.

products.name: Descript
products.why: AI clips with human criteria first: clip count, duration, layout and an optional topic are set before Submit, and clip bounds stay editable as transcript text.

products.name: Frame.io
products.why: Share settings sit in a sidebar next to the video: expiry presets (24 hours, 1 week, 2 weeks) above a calendar, a passphrase, and a separate Downloads toggle.

products.name: Dropbox
products.why: The deepest link policy: separate view and edit links, expiry, password and disable-downloads, an honest scope warning, and a 'Restrictions apply' cue under Copy link after saving.

products.name: ClassDojo
products.why: Group-first feedback: award a rubric-like skill to a whole group in one tap with a big confirmation and Undo, then a whole-class report that drills into each learner with a dated log.

products.name: Beside
products.why: A dedicated in-person recorder with a floating widget that keeps recording while you navigate, ending in an overview with transcript and AI to-dos: the phone voice-memo fallback. No consent prompt is shown.

products.name: Google Maps
products.why: The only 360 look-around evidence found: an immersive view split with a 2D map whose peg shows where you are facing, plus switching capture dates without leaving 360.

products.name: DAZN
products.why: A related-highlights shelf directly under the main player, with −10s skip and a Watch now / Share sheet. Fetched for camera switching, but the screens show none.

patterns.title: AI claims link to the moment that proves them
patterns.body: Grain, Fireflies and Otter all attach timestamps to AI summary items (outcomes, action items, outline entries), and a click jumps both video and transcript. This is the mechanism for 'evidence-linked moments' in an AI debrief and maps directly onto the SRV's clickable AI annotation markers. None of the three puts an approval step between the AI text and the Share button.

patterns.title: Human gates sit before generation or at publish, not after the summary
patterns.body: The review steps found are at the edges: Fireflies makes you preview a custom AI prompt on at least two past meetings before it runs, Descript asks for clip count, duration and topic before Submit, and Fireflies soundbites need a title and an access level before Done. AI summaries themselves (Grain, Otter web) go straight to Share. Essentials needs both: faculty criteria up front and an explicit reveal before learners or the big screen see AI output.

patterns.title: The big screen shows join chrome briefly; control lives on the phone
patterns.body: Canva's presenting screen shows a QR, a short code for phones that won't scan, a live participant count and a Hide toggle to clear the banner once people have joined. Its phone flow and Google TV's put transport controls, scrubbing and connection status on the phone only, so the shared display stays clean. No single flow shows both sides at once; Canva's two flows together come closest.

patterns.title: Share policy is set beside the video, with expiry presets and a separate download switch
patterns.body: Frame.io keeps share settings in a sidebar next to playback with relative expiry presets; Dropbox splits view from edit links and confirms 'Restrictions apply' after saving; Fireflies asks who can access a clip at the moment it is created. All three treat download as its own toggle, separate from viewing. None shows a consent or confirmation step before the download itself.

patterns.title: Group-first feedback and individual rubrics are separate products today
patterns.body: ClassDojo awards one skill to a whole group in a single tap, confirms it large with Undo, and reports whole-class first with per-learner drill-down. Grain scores one speaker at a time against a rubric under the video and sends the result to that person. Essentials' dominant mode needs ClassDojo's group default with Grain's rubric and per-person override in the same screen; no product shows the combination.

patterns.title: Phone capture keeps recording in the background and accepts markers while live
patterns.body: Otter shows a live transcript with one-tap highlight, comment and photo markers during recording; Beside offers a dedicated in-person mode and a floating recorder that survives navigation. Both end in an overview (summary, transcript, to-dos) attached to the conversation record. This is the pattern for capturing the debrief discussion on the faculty phone; neither asks participants for consent.

patterns.title: Speaker-aware transcripts double as a participation view
patterns.body: Grain colours transcript speakers to match a talk-time timeline under the video; Otter shows talk-time percentages and lets you rematch mis-attributed speakers. In a team simulation this is formative data (who led, who stayed silent), and speaker correction matters because AI attribution in a noisy sim room will be wrong.

open_questions: Camera views is an honest gap: no Mobbin or Refero flow shows switching between camera angles or controlling a PTZ camera during playback of a recording. DAZN and Tesla were fetched for this but show a highlights shelf and a clip library. Google Maps is the only 360 evidence and it is free outdoor roaming, not a fixed room on a timeline (mobbin:337a0dfd-6591-4af6-97b3-397dcc6eac6f). Multi-camera sim review needs its own prototype or research outside these sources.

No source shows the full second-screen handoff in one flow, and none shows private notes on the phone while the shared screen stays clean; Canva and Google TV only show remote control (mobbin:f28f8936-895b-450a-8e9b-5a83c12ba692, mobbin:3f1ac467-e548-499a-91bf-cd1e5a74aea6). All phone-side evidence is phone-sized, so the tablet-versus-phone conflict is not settled by this research.

What should 'faculty approve' mean with a group waiting in the debrief room? Every AI summary observed shares immediately (mobbin:c2a5d587-f496-4eb4-bc78-509bd3c32787, mobbin:2523ca18-b9ac-4576-8555-a20d27016d3e); the gates found are at setup or clip level. Per-item reveal on the big screen versus everything hidden until an explicit release is untested.

Consent is missing everywhere: Beside and Otter start recording an in-person conversation without a consent prompt (mobbin:b5d1550e-5945-48c2-97c4-e12e9ea63dc4, mobbin:d7a0fc7c-713c-40b5-bbc4-4447ba7e6a8f), and Dropbox and Frame.io can disable downloads but show no confirm-before-download step (mobbin:8fee942f-3bba-4b19-949e-9011dfee633f). Both the recording-faculty-speech consent and the download consent need original design.

ClassDojo's group feedback is behaviour points for school children and Grain's scorecard grades one person (mobbin:b83099d3-97b5-452a-ab79-cece306cc444, mobbin:6b6443d7-dcb9-4e6e-b6a1-d82455a1fae9). How a group rubric with per-person overrides is stored, reported and released to each learner is open.

Timing of AI clips is not evidenced: Descript and Fireflies generate clips from recordings that already exist, and no screen shows how long generation takes (mobbin:71f5995e-099a-4f4a-ac23-6e4d884cf1f2, mobbin:0384c559-2a2e-4a37-9cb8-7be772d37a27). The 'clips ready immediately after the session' constraint needs a technical answer, not a UI one.
